text:
alex: Heads-up, after the kernel-selector change on canary last night I'm seeing steady GPU memory "pad" growth across long-running continuous-batching workloads. Started at ~0100 UTC, reproduced on two clusters.

sara: Any OOMs observed or just higher baseline?

alex: No hard OOMs yet, but padding waste up ~12% and workspace high-water mark creeping. p99 token latency unchanged but p95 jittered.

diego: Do you have the batch-size distribution? Could be the new kernel's alignment behavior.

alex: Here's an excerpt from the profiler and the allocator slab stats:

```
Batch stats: median_seq=64, tail_seq=512, avg_batch=7.2
Kernel: tiled-attn-v2 -> selected when seq>128
Pad waste delta: +12.1% after 03:00 deploy
Slab occupancy: 78% -> 91% (24h)
Workspace highwater: 9.4GB -> 10.6GB
KV-cache shadow allocations: small transient peaks correlated with longer sequences
```

jen: "KV-cache shadow allocations" — can you expand? Is it KV duplication or shadow buffers during kernel fallback?

alex: Looks like when kernel selector switches to tiled-attn-v2 it allocates a temporary workspace that doesn't reuse the allocator's pinned slab buckets. The memory is reclaimed, but the pad accounting still treats the batch as if full-width, so padding ledger spikes.

mike: Can you paste the allocation trace (short)?

alex: clipped trace: `allocator.slab_alloc(bucket=32MB) -> workspace.temp_alloc(8MB) -> kv.shadow_alloc(6MB) -> free(kv)` repeated per long sequence. Pattern repeats across ~300 requests/min.

sara: Possible fixes: 1) make kernel allocate from the same slab buckets, 2) decrement pad accounting during ephemeral allocations, or 3) adjust sequence-weighted batching so large sequences go to dedicated lanes. Thoughts?

diego: I like (2) + better telemetry first. Add two counters: `ephemeral_alloc_bytes` and `pad_at_alloc_time`. If we can correlate per-batch pad vs ephemeral, we'll know what to change safely.

jen: Also consider lowering the tiled-attn-v2 activation threshold temporarily (seq>256 -> seq>192) to avoid frequent switching for borderline traces. That might reduce shadowing.

mike: If we go (1) kernel-side, need a small runtime patch: accept an allocator token or allocator-view for temp buffers. Low-risk but touches kernel API.

alex: Quick experiment I ran: forced tiled-attn-v2 off for 2h on canary — pad waste reverted to baseline, slab occupancy normalized. So selector flip is the proximate cause.

sara: OK action items:
- diego: add telemetry (ephemeral_alloc_bytes, pad_at_alloc_time, kernel_select_count) — quick PR, add to per-model dashboard.
- mike: prototype allocator-view API for kernels (small RFC).
- jen: change selector threshold to 192 for canary tomorrow and monitor.
- alex: run a targeted replay against long-chat traces with both kernels and capture allocation traces.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/patch/selector-threshold -> in progress (will notify on completion) :gear:

diego: I'll start the telemetry PR now. Planning to include a small flamegraph snippet in the payload.

mike: I'll draft the allocator-view RFC and include compatibility notes for current kernels.

alex: Thanks — please flag if telemetry shows ephemeral allocations > 5% of pad for sustained periods. If so we'll revert selector and ship kernel patch.

sara: Also let's add a regression test in the batching-sim harness that simulates seq-drift and ensures pad waste < 10% for 99th percentile workloads.

alex: Sounds good. I'll upload traces and results to the thread when done.

jen: small note — check model quantization path too, some kernels have different workspace footprints depending on quant path. Might be an orthogonal contributor.

mike: agreed. I'll call that out in RFC.

alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
